title: Massachusetts Will Vote on Allowing Smaller Homes
summary:
Homes in Massachusetts cost a lot of money. Now voters there will decide on a plan to make it easier to build smaller, cheaper homes.

Many towns have rules about how big a piece of land a house must sit on. In Massachusetts, most of these rules say at least an acre. That is almost as big as a football field.

The plan would let homes be built on land as small as 5,000 square feet. That is about the size of a basketball court. The plan would not apply to Boston.

People who support it say big land rules mean fewer homes, and the homes that get built are large and expensive. Housing expert Andrew Mikula is leading the push. Polls suggest many people support it.

People against the plan say towns should make their own rules. They also doubt the homes would really be cheap. One older house on a small lot was for sale for nearly $1.3 million.
why_it_matters: Rules like this can decide whether families, maybe even yours someday, can afford a home in the town they love.
